sentences.text: Hans works hard for seven years.
He receives a big piece of gold as pay.
Hans puts the gold on his shoulder and starts to walk home to his mother.
The gold is very heavy.
Hans sees a man on a horse.
"Riding looks easy," says Hans.
The man stops and says, "Give me your gold, and I will give you my horse."
Hans is happy to trade.
Hans gets on the horse, but the horse runs too fast.
He falls to the ground.
A farmer with a cow helps him stand up.
"Horses are dangerous," says Hans.
"I like your cow.
It gives milk every day."
The farmer smiles and says, "I will trade my cow for your horse."
Hans agrees right away.
Hans walks with the cow.
He feels very thirsty and tries to get milk.
But no milk comes out.
The cow kicks Hans, and he falls down.
A man with a pig sees him.
"That cow is too old to give milk," says the man.
"Your pig looks young and good," says Hans.
"I can trade my pig for the cow," says the man.
Hans agrees to the trade.
Later, Hans meets a boy with a white goose.
Hans tells the boy about his lucky trades.
The boy says, "My goose is very heavy.
The meat will be good."
"My pig is good, too," says Hans.
Then the boy says, "Is that pig yours?
A rich man is looking for his lost pig.
It is missing.
You may be in trouble."
Hans feels afraid.
"Please help me," he says.
"Take this pig and give me your goose."
Hans thinks he is very lucky with the big goose.
In the next village, he sees a man with a large stone.
The man uses the stone for his work.
The man sings while he works.
"You look happy," says Hans.
The man says, "My work brings me money.
You can do this work, too."
"How can I do that?" asks Hans.
"You just need a stone," says the man.
"Take this goose and give me your stone," says Hans.
"Now I will be rich," Hans thinks.
But the stone is very heavy.
Soon, Hans feels tired and hungry.
Hans stops at a well to drink water.
He puts the stone on the edge.
By accident, he pushes the stone.
Splash!
It falls into the deep water.
He jumps for joy.
"Thank my lucky stars!" he shouts.
"The heavy stone is gone.
I am free from this heavy weight."
Now he has nothing left.
He has no gold, no horse, and no stone.
But he is the happiest man in the world.
